newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Israel Knesset urges Lithuania act on war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Israel Knesset urges Lithuania act on war crimes.

text.p: A letter signed by 92 of 120 Israeli Knesset members has been sent to Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas urging him to ensure the prosecution of alleged war criminals, Nazi-hunters said on Thursday.
The letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, was organised by the Simon Wiesenthal Centre in Jerusalem and will be presented to Brazauskas on Friday.
It calls on the president to honour a promise he made to the Knesset two years ago during a visit to Israel when he vowed the Baltic state would take action against alleged war criminals.
"We call upon you to honour your promise to the people of Israel that those responsible for these terrible crimes be held accountable," the letter said.
Lithuania has been criticised since regaining independence from the former Soviet Union in 1991 for failing to prosecute people alleged to have taken part in Nazi atrocities.
Historians estimate that 94 percent of the 220,000 Jews living in Lithuania before World War Two were murdered during the Nazi Holocaust.
The letter noted that not one alleged war criminal had been brought to trial although five were now living in Lithuania.
The most notorious of the alleged war criminals is Aleksandras Lileikis, who was last year stripped of his U.S. citizenship on the grounds he concealed his war-time activities.
U.S. prosecutors say he handed over scores of Jews to Nazi death squads when he was head of the security police in Nazi-occupied Vilnius. Lileikis, 89, denies the charges.
Lileikis' second-in-command, Kazys Gimzauskas, 88, has also been mentioned by Nazi hunters.
"Months have passed since Lileikis ran away to Lithuania and he has still not been arrested let alone put on trial, despite the overwhelming evidence against him," the letter added.
Efraim Zhuroff, the director of the Simon Wiesenthal Centre, said the fact that so many Knesset members signed the letter showed the anger felt in Israel at Lithuania's inaction.
"The fact that President Brazauskas publicly promised his country would do so adds salt to the wounds of the survivors and their families," Zhuroff told Reuters.
